stories.headline: Who comes out ahead in Dylan Larkin blockbuster? Grading the Red Wings, Canadiens
stories.summary: Hockey trade season is heating up! Find grades for each GM involved in all the big swaps here.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season opened Sept. 29, but teams did not wait until the opening puck drop to start improving their rosters.

The Maple Leafs and Blue Jackets completed a trade Sept. 28 that involved six players, most notably sending Kirill Marchenko to Toronto and Matthew Knies to Columbus.

Oct. 23, the long-anticipated Connor Hellebuyck trade finally happened, as he landed with the Devils. And on Nov. 1, the Kraken and Predators swapped young forwards (Shane Wright for Matthew Wood).

The most recent trade was a blockbuster, with Dylan Larkin headed from Detroit to Montreal.

Throughout the season, this page will be your home for analysis of all the big deals by ESPN reporters, with the most recent swaps at the top.

Jump to:

Larkin to MTL

Wright to NSH

Hellebuyck to NJ

Marchenko to TOR

Nov. 22: Red Wings send Larkin to Montreal
Larkin finally has a new home with the Detroit Red Wings trading the star center to the Montreal Canadiens.

Larkin, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round pick are heading to the Canadiens with forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, prospect forward Michael Hage, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2029 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick.

Here's a look at what the NHL's latest blockbuster trade means for all parties involved:

Detroit Red Wings

Grade: A+
Finding the best possible deal that hypothetically helps your organization right now and in the future becomes the focal point for any front office that has a star player who wants out. This was the objective facing Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff when it came to Larkin and finding what he felt was the best deal.

Getting to this point took time because Horcoff and the Red Wings knew they couldn't let a legitimate top-six two-way center with four years remaining on his contract leave for a minuscule return. It had to be something substantial.

Horcoff and the Red Wings found something that's substantial for many reasons.

Detroit entered Sunday nine points adrift of the second and final Eastern Conference wild-card spot four days before American Thanksgiving. It's not to say that a turnaround to push for a postseason place is or was impossible. But it is a major undertaking that forces any team that's in that situation to be honest about their circumstances. The Red Wings are six points better than the Vancouver Canucks for the fewest points in the league, meaning they are closer to the lottery than the postseason at this stage.

It's what made receiving draft capital or any young players who can be part of the next steps for the Red Wings pivotal.

Receiving Hage, a junior at the University of Michigan, along with two first-round picks in a haul that includes four draft picks allows the Red Wings to further supplement whatever lies ahead. Hage, a first-round pick in 2024, was one of the Canadiens' top prospects. He's a playmaking center that is averaging 2.0 points per game this season for the Wolverines. His first two years in Ann Arbor have seen him average more than a point per game. There's also what he's done for Team USA at the World Juniors in which he had 15 points in seven games.

Getting one of, if not, the top prospect in the Canadiens' system strengthens a Red Wings setup that was arguably lacking that top-six forward. They have forwards like Nate Danielson, Eddie Genborg and J.P. Hurlbert that appear as if they project as NHL players. But having Hage further amplifies what the Wings have coming in the future when it comes to their top-six.

Another item that should help with bolstering that farm system is the draft capital that arrived in the trade. The Red Wings are going to have two first-round picks in two of the next three draft cycles. Getting a second-round pick in this year's draft helps given they moved on from their original second-rounder in a previous deal.

Dach, the No. 3 pick in 2019, has a chance to potentially find a consistent place with the third team he'll play for since making his debut back in the 2019-20 season. Injuries, among other items, have impacted Dach when it comes to figuring out where he fits in a team's overall scheme. It's likely the Red Wings will use him as a top-nine forward that's capable of providing some secondary or tertiary production. He has two goals and eight points in 22 games with five of those points coming in his last nine games.

Montembeault has yet to feature this season after sustaining a lower-body injury in practice in early October. He's been on injured reserve since then with the belief he'll return at some point. His arrival will provide the Red Wings with another option in net which could prove useful. John Gibson came into Sunday at 4-8-1 with a 3.54 goals-against average and a .862 save percentage. That has been a contrast compared to Daniil Tarasov, who is 3-4-2 but possesses a 1.98 GAA and a .927 save percentage through his first 10 games.

Montreal Canadiens

Grade: A

Not that there ever were any allusions about the Canadiens at this point. But if there were, then, let's be clear. They're trying to win a Stanley Cup right now and for the foreseeable future because a trade like this isn't executed out of boredom.

And if we're being even more direct here: That's exactly what Larkin said he wanted.

Montreal had always been floated as a potential destination. But there were the questions about whether Larkin would want to play for a Canadian team. Then again? Does location really matter if the goal for the player who wants out of their situation is to win?

It clearly didn't with TSN reporting late Sunday that Larkin was open to going to Montreal for more than two months. But the Canadiens wanted to "keep that quiet" because they felt it could potentially disrupt the trade from getting done. It's something Larkin's camp agreed with but that also came with the context that getting Hage was a priority for the Red Wings.

The Canadiens being in the market for Larkin made too much sense. Larkin wanted to play for a team that has a chance to win right now and beyond. The Red Wings wanted to find a trade partner they felt could give them something that was too enticing to turn down. The Canadiens met all those requirements by being a young team that has the cap space, the draft capital, the prospect base and roster players that could make a deal happen.

What Larkin provides them is a proven top-line center that has authored five consecutive 30-goal seasons, who also features a two-way ability that can see him be used to create matchup problems.

Now he's going to Montreal, where he'll likely be the second-line center behind the reigning Selke Trophy winner in Nick Suzuki, forming a top-six dynamic down the middle that is going to give Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis options. That's part of a larger composite that includes another proven two-way center with Phillip Danault on the third line with Jake Evans on the bottom line.

That makes the Canadiens as formidable as any team in the NHL when it comes to what they can do down the middle with their personnel.

Obtaining that, however, comes with a cost. Larkin is under contract for four more years at $8.7 million annually. But it's another reason why the Canadiens made too much sense. They could afford it because their front office already had their core of Cole Caufield, Ivan Demidov, Jakub Dobes, Noah Dobson, Kaiden Guhle, Lane Hutson, Mike Matheson, Alex Newhook and Juraj Slafkovsky signed to contracts that are at least three years in length.

Having several forwards signed is what made Dach expendable. The emergence of Jacob Fowler this season and the notion Dobes can work toward attaining consistency is also what made Montreal feel comfortable with trading a goalie. Being a playoff team that's trying to be a perennial Stanley Cup favorite means getting help and the way teams have done that is by bartering the first-round picks that helped them get in his position in the first place.

Where it gets interesting, however, is the discussion around Hage. Some will argue that a prospect averaging more than a point per game throughout two-plus years of college hockey is someone to keep because they can help you win. Others will argue that having someone like that can help you win ... right now if you trade them for someone that is more proven in nature, which applies to Larkin.

Nov. 1: Wright to Nashville, Wood to Seattle
Two players once central to their former franchise's plans were moved Sunday in a deal involving the Nashville Predators and the Seattle Kraken.

The Predators traded winger Matthew Wood to the Kraken for center Shane Wright. The trade was a one-for-one swap involving two teams already vying for a playoff spot.

Here's a quick glance at what it all means.

Nashville Predators

Grade: B+
Any time two forwards in their early 20s are traded for each other, "potential" will be used a lot to describe the move.

Wood and Wright struggled to start the season. Wood has three points in 14 games, and Wright has four in 14. But the Predators might have acquired the player with fewer questions.

Wright has been the subject of trade rumors the past few years because of the potential he showed as a draft prospect, being selected fourth in 2022, and his output during the 2024-25 season (19 goals and 44 points in 79 games). It was a strong baseline for a player who previously had 16 games of NHL experience over the previous two years because of a stop-start development process.

Despite having only 12 goals and 27 points the next season, he proved he can score in double figures in back-to-back seasons. Furthermore, he recorded double figures for a team that, over a two-year span, has been in the bottom 10 of goals per game.

It's likely that Nashville will slot Wright in as the second-line center, with Ryan O'Reilly, Jack Drury and Alexander Kerfoot as the other pivots. The Predators are hoping to return to the playoffs for the first time since 2024, when they were eliminated in the first round.

Seattle Kraken

Grade: B+
Wright became expendable for a few reasons, including inconsistencies since that promising 19-goal campaign and the fact that the Kraken have more productive options down the middle. Berkly Catton is second on the team in points (11), while Frederick Gaudreau leads the Kraken in goals (seven). Matty Beniers is averaging 0.50 points per game while logging the most ice time (17:43 per game) among Kraken forwards. Chandler Stephenson, a natural center, has gone to wing and leads the Kraken with 12 points in 14 games.

Adding Wood provides the Kraken a natural winger who can provide secondary production while also adding some size on the wing; the former University of Connecticut star is listed at 6-foot-4 and 202 pounds. He is also adept at using his size to get to the net front.

Wood scored 17 goals and 30 points in his first full NHL season in 2025-26, and there's potential for more. He can also fit within the Kraken's team construct. Though Wood shoots from the perimeter, he is effective enough at getting into the low slot and net front too.

Pairing him with playmaking forwards such as Beniers, Catton, Gaudreau and Stephenson, along with puck-moving defensemen such as Vince Dunn and Brandon Montour, could lead to him hitting the 20-goal benchmark.

Oct. 23: Hellebuyck lands with Devils
Technically speaking, Connor Hellebuyck's suspension from the Winnipeg Jets did end Friday. It just had a different outcome with the three-time Vezina Trophy winner being traded to the New Jersey Devils.

Hellebuyck, who won the Hart Trophy in 2025, will go to the Devils in exchange for forward Dawson Mercer, forward Nick Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, prospect center Alexander Command, a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Let's take a look at what this means for both teams and how each front office performed:

New Jersey Devils

Grade: A
How Devils general manager Sunny Mehta arrived at this place goes back to one of his earliest moves. He knew the going rate to acquire a starting goaltender based on the return New Jersey received in late June when Mehta traded Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers. Markstrom's trade brought back a return of three forwards. It was a move that gave Mehta, or any GM, more insight into what it would take to land arguably the greatest goaltender of his generation in Hellebuyck.

Trading Markstrom is also the reason acquiring Hellebuyck -- or any proven No. 1 goalie -- became a priority for New Jersey. That became even more evident with how the Devils started the regular season. Opening their first 10 games with a goaltending tandem of Jake Allen and Daws had the Devils entering Friday in the second and final Eastern Conference wild-card spot -- with the context that they appear to be a much better team than their place in the standings shows.

New Jersey has one of the strongest defensive structures in the NHL this season. The Devils came into the weekend allowing the second-fewest high-danger scoring chances per 60, the third-fewest scoring chances per 60, and the 10th-fewest shots per 60.

They also have a 59.74% shot share in 5-on-5 play. That figure is so strong that only the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes (59.79% shot share) have held on to the puck more than the Devils in 5-on-5 play. So how is it that a team that controls the puck and limits high-danger chances, scoring chances and shots is in the last wild-card spot? Especially when it averages the 12th-most goals per game?

An argument could be had that it's because of the Devils' goaltending. They have the 13th-lowest team save percentage in 5-on-5 play at 89.95%. Across all scenarios, they have an .880 team save percentage, tied for the 23rd in the league.

Placing Hellebuyck, who has faced the second-most shots in the NHL since 2021-22, in New Jersey's system could see the Devils win more frequently by pairing his skills with their defensive infrastructure. And if it does? That's the possibility that Mehta and the Devils are banking on: that Hellebuyck can help them emerge as a legitimate threat to challenge in the Eastern Conference and perhaps have serious designs on winning a Stanley Cup this season.

That's the short-term view of how this can be digested. The long-term view is that the Devils, barring some sort of massive change, are going to be expected to challenge for a Stanley Cup with the 33-year-old Hellebuyck under contract for four more years at $8.5 million annually.

Building around homegrown talents such as Jesper Bratt, Nico Hischier and Jack Hughes has been a process. The Devils have used a variety of avenues from free agency to trades to build what they believe is the best possible team around a core that has since added another homegrown player in Luke Hughes. There have been times when the Devils look like they've been ready to aspire to more. But then there have been those moments when they've been left to ask probing questions about how they reach their desired destination.

Getting Hellebuyck has changed the conversation. Hellebuyck missing training camp because of his suspension means there is likely going to be an adjustment period. Nonetheless, adding the best version of Hellebuyck to a team that has proved it can consistently score and defend makes the Devils look like they're on the verge of something major. But the regular season, while important, isn't where this trade will ultimately be judged. The verdict will come in the playoffs, as the franchise seeks to win a Stanley Cup -- one of the few accolades Hellebuyck doesn't already have in his collection.

Winnipeg Jets

Grade: B+
Any deal Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff was going to reach for Hellebuyck was one that had to help the franchise both immediately and for the foreseeable future. It appears this particular trade has a chance to do both, with the caveat that it was always going to be a challenge to find the perfect return for the best player the Jets have drafted over the past 20 years.

That's why the place to start is with what it could mean for the Jets right now. Scoring was so much of an issue for the Jets in the 2025-26 season that three players -- Kyle Connor, Mark Scheifele and Gabriel Vilardi -- combined to score 40% of Winnipeg's goals. It was a drastic contrast compared with the 2024-25 season, when the Jets won the Presidents' Trophy largely due to contributions from different parts of their lineup.

Scoring, at least to start the season, remains an issue. The Jets came into Friday ranking 25th in the league in goals per game at a rate of 2.60 per contest. Adding to those scoring challenges is how they've struggled to consistently create opportunities when they've had the puck. They are averaging the 12th-fewest shots per 60, the 13th-fewest scoring chances per 60 and remain around league average in terms of high-danger chances per 60. Plus, the Jets have the 11th-lowest shot share in 5-on-5 play at 47.30%.

Expecting Mercer to be the lone solution to those problems isn't realistic. But it's fair to expect that he'll help by providing another option beyond Connor, Scheifele and Vilardi. Mercer is a three-time 20-goal scorer who finished last season with 20 goals and 42 points while averaging 18:13 in ice time. That level of production would have made him the Jets' fourth-leading goal scorer and had him fifth on the team in points.

Mercer, who has one year of team control remaining after this season, has zero goals and four assists through 10 games. The 24-year-old's ability to attain consistency is likely going to play an important role in a campaign that appears already to be at a sensitive stage. Winnipeg entered Friday with the same points total as the Colorado Avalanche for the second and final Western Conference wild-card spot.

The Avalanche have a Central Division-leading plus-10 goal differential. The four teams in the division that are either tied with or ahead of the Jets in the standings also have positive goal differentials, whereas the Jets currently sit at minus-3, having lost their past four games.

Bjugstad, who had six goals and nine points in 61 games last season, is still recovering from offseason pectoral muscle surgery that saw him begin the season on injured reserve. His initial diagnosis had him set to return at some point in the next four to six months, which places his earliest return around January. Bjugstad is in the final year of his contract, and it's possible he could once again be a deadline day departure should the Jets seek draft capital if they're out of the playoff chase. The Jets have 28 draft picks over the next three years after the Hellebuyck trade.

Daws, who is 2-2 with a 2.78 goals-against average and a .874 save percentage, is joining a team that has the fourth-highest save percentage in 5-on-5 play. He provides the Jets with a more proven alternative in net should they need it. The Jets have used Clay Stevenson in tandem with Stuart Skinner, but Stevenson came into this season with five games of NHL experience, whereas Daws already had 55 games and is more than familiar with the demands of being in a tandem at this level.

Getting Command, the 12th pick in the 2026 draft, gives the Jets another potential top-six or top-nine option for the future as he continues to develop in Sweden. Command has seven goals and 12 points playing in the under-20 Nationell against younger competition, while he has no points in six games while playing for Orebro in the Swedish Hockey League, the strongest league in the Swedish hockey system.

Sept. 28: Marchenko to the Leafs, Knies to the Blue Jackets
Less than 24 hours before the start of a new season, the NHL had its first blockbuster trade with the Blue Jackets trading Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs.

Marchenko, along with forward Miles Wood and goaltender Elvis Merzlikins, heads to Toronto in exchange for forwards Matthew Knies and Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae and a conditional 2027 second-round pick. Columbus will retain 18% of Merzlikins' salary.

Here's a look at how both teams fared:

Toronto Maple Leafs

Grade: A-
Maybe the easiest -- and most important -- place to start is with Marchenko signing a six-year contract carrying a $12.5 million average annual value. Attaining cost certainty is always going to be key for teams, especially in this current landscape in which the price for a player's services is subject to change with each new contract. This holds true for Marchenko.

He was under contract for one more year at $3.85 million, and one more year of team control as a pending restricted free agent. That left any team acquiring him facing one of two hypotheticals:

Would it be better for them to trade for Marchenko, let him play out the season, see how he looks in their lineup and then sign him to a long-term deal?
Or do they get a sign-and-trade done so they have him locked in for several years at what they believe is a manageable cost -- at a time when every class of player is going to cash in, with top-line players at the top of that list?

Choosing the second option allowed the Leafs to avoid the seasonlong dilemma of deliberating on a long-term deal. That could prove to be a vital decision, with the expectation that Marchenko's stats are likely to surge while playing alongside Auston Matthews for at least two seasons. Because although Marchenko played with talented centers in his time with the Blue Jackets, some believe he could reach the 40-goal mark for the first time in his career playing with the Leafs superstar. His career high is 31, scored in 2024-25.

His addition sets the Leafs up to have a first line with Jack Roslovic joining Matthews and Marchenko, while having a second line featuring William Nylander, John Tavares and rookie Gavin McKenna, the Penn State forward who was the first pick in the 2026 draft.

Matthews' future is another subject for another time. Yet when it comes to Marchenko? Getting him signed long term provides the Leafs with more certainty. He is the seventh player on their active roster who has more than three years of team control remaining.

Other elements of this trade will come under question. That starts with whether it was prudent to add more to their salary cap starting next season knowing Knies, who is entering the second year of a six-year contract, was already on the roster at a cheaper salary of $7.75 million annually.

Then there are Merzlikins and Wood. Merzlikins is currently on IR after undergoing offseason shoulder surgery. He's in the final year of his contract worth $4.428 million. When healthy, he's another option for the Leafs in goal. But they could also move on from him later in the season to get help elsewhere. Wood, who went unclaimed on waivers, gives the Leafs a potential depth forward if needed.

Columbus Blue Jackets

Grade: B+
There's a challenge facing every front office that has a star player who wants out of town. Of course there will be other teams who want the player in question. Whether any of the proposed deals make sense usually ends up being the biggest hurdle to clear.

That's what makes this particular trade for the Blue Jackets one that could work. Why? Because of how they stand to benefit both now and in the future.

Moving on from Marchenko, who led the Blue Jackets with 27 goals and was second with 67 points last season, meant Columbus had to find a comparable winger in return. Knies appears to be just that. The 23-year-old, who had 23 goals and 66 points last season, gives the Blue Jackets a sizable option on the edge who can generate offensive opportunities in a top-six role. Knies will face questions about how his production will fare without Matthews, but his ability to attack the net could prove critical for a Columbus team that was in the top 10 in scoring chances per 60 minutes but was around league average in high-danger chances per 60.

Columbus could use Knies on its top line next to Adam Fantilli and Kent Johnson, while having a second line featuring Conor Garland, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin, who arrived this summer in trade.

Knies' $7.75 million AAV also helps, as Fantilli is set to earn $13.75 million annually starting this season. In total, Columbus has seven players set to make more than $7 million annually who have four or more years left on their current deals.

Beyond Knies, Lorentz provides the Blue Jackets with another proven option they can use in various spots as needed. He scored seven goals and 18 points in 71 games last season after eight and 19 in 2024-25, his first campaign with the Leafs. And while the Blue Jackets do have a bottom six in place, Lorentz gives them someone who logged more than 158 short-handed minutes last season; this could prove beneficial for a team that was 28th on the penalty kill last season.

Emil Andrae -- who was already traded once this offseason, from Philly back on June 16 -- is an option on the back end. He had 13 points in 61 games with the Flyers last season.

stories.headline: NFL Week 11: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 11.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season began with several blowouts.

With Josh Johnson at quarterback, the Cardinals couldn't get anything going offensively in a loss to the Chiefs. Miami also struggled on that side of the ball against Buffalo in quarterback Kyle McCord's second start. And the Titans' defense allowed touchdowns on the Cowboys' first six drives, leading to a 21-point defeat.

Elsewhere in the early window, the Panthers came out on top of a shootout against the Ravens. The Eagles pulled off an upset over the Steelers with backup quarterback Joe Milton. The Bears won their fifth straight game, while the Lions won in their first game without edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee injury) this season.

In the late window, both New York teams pulled off wins. And Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza almost came back against the Broncos, but a pick-six ended a potential go-ahead drive late in the fourth quarter. The 49ers capped things off Sunday night with a resounding win over the Vikings in Mexico City.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

MIN-SF | JAX-NYG | LV-DEN

NYJ-LAC | BAL-CAR

NO-CHI | PIT-PHI | TB-DET

TEN-DAL | MIA-BUF | ARI-KC

Catch up on Thursday's game:

IND-HOU

San Francisco 35, Minnesota 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap | Instant analysis

49ers
Is the 49ers' pass rush ready to take off? The 49ers' defensive line has caught plenty of recent flak for a lack of pressure and production. During their week of practice in Colorado Springs, edge rusher Nick Bosa vowed that he would be better and so, too, would the defensive front. Bosa was right, as the Niners harassed Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins for much of the night. Bosa collected his first sack of the season, and the 49ers' pressure forced several errant Cousins throws, including safety Ji'Ayir Brown's pick-6. The Niners finished with one sack but affected Cousins consistently for most of the night. The Niners pressured Cousins on 15 of 39 dropbacks and he averaged 4.0 yards per attempt with an interceptions and a sack when San Francisco didn't blitz.

What to make of the QB performance: Brock Purdy undoubtedly heard all the doubts about how he'd fare against Brian Flores' exotic defense after a couple of rough outings previously. But coach Kyle Shanahan said this week that Purdy's previous experience playing against that scheme should help him and that Purdy wouldn't be surprised by anything that Flores could throw at him. That proved true Sunday night, as Purdy finished 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. That included 17-of-19 against the blitz with two touchdowns and 12 first downs on the 20 dropbacks in which Minnesota brought five or more pass rushers. -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Vikings
What should we take from Kirk Cousins' second start? At one point in the first half, Cousins appeared to be telling right tackle Brian O'Neill that he was being hit on every dropback. Heavy pressure eventually limited the Vikings' attempts to push the ball downfield and made it all but impossible to mount a comeback. Cousins has added a higher level of accuracy and decision-making to the Vikings' offense in his two-game stint, but the 49ers' pass rush, which sacked him once, made him frenetic.

Most surprising performance: The Vikings absorbed a blow pregame when cornerback Isaiah Rodgers was declared inactive because of a quad injury he suffered in practice. And while Rodgers' absence alone was not the sole cause, the defense appeared uncomfortable and on its heels from the start. Purdy did what no other opposing quarterback had been able to do this season: find the parts of the field vacated by the Vikings' blitz packages. Purdy faced the Vikings' blitz on 20 of his first 26 dropbacks, and he completed 89% of his passes in those situations for two touchdowns and 12 first downs. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: vs. Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Justin Jefferson scored 13.7 points in the Sunday night loss to the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 87 receiving yards. Jefferson did lose a fumble, but he's now brought in 16 of 22 targets for 160 yards in the two games played with Cousins at quarterback. With a favorable upcoming schedule (ATL, CAR, @NE), Jefferson is set-up to produce consistent WR1 numbers. -- Bowen

N.Y. Giants 23, Jacksonville 18
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
Are the Giants for real? This was putting the rest of the NFL on notice, even good teams. Playing coach John Harbaugh's Giants is not going to be easy. New York thoroughly beat the Jaguars at home for its first win this season against a team with a winning record at the time. It was a statement game for these Giants, especially for a defense that held Jacksonville to one touchdown in six red zone trips and forced two Trevor Lawrence interceptions. After a week when they clearly didn't like the idea that they were overmatched against good teams, this was proof that they belong -- and they are heavy favorites to win the NFC East.

Most surprising performance: LB Abdul Carter. The pressure finally paid off with sacks. The second-year edge rusher came into Sunday with two sacks this season despite being second in the NFL in pass rush win rate. He doubled that sack total by halftime and finished with five QB hits. Carter and the Giants had Lawrence under pressure all afternoon. -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: at Colts (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jaguars
Was this offensive performance an aberration or a troubling sign for the rest of the season? The Jaguars scored only one touchdown after putting up 115 points in the past three weeks. In six trips to the red zone, they had the one TD, four field goals and one turnover on downs. They already entered Sunday without center Robert Hainsey (knee). Then in the second half, left tackle Walker Little went down with a knee injury. The Jaguars have bounced back from bad performances before -- they put up 35 points the week after scoring just 13 in Denver -- and the Jaguars get a good matchup against Tennessee, which allowed 51 points to Dallas on Sunday.

What to make of the QB performance: Lawrence topped 300 yards, but this was one of his worst performances of the past two-plus seasons. He was under heavy pressure (hit five times and sacked three times in the first half) and his receivers were unable to get much separation, but his two interceptions came on under- and over-thrown passes. It's the first time he has thrown multiple interceptions in a game since an overtime victory over Arizona in Week 12 last season. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten (who has been dealing with ankle and foot injuries) scored 8.3 fantasy points and played only 43% of the snaps. It's fair to question whether the ailments are hindering his performance, as he has totaled 53 fewer rushing yards than expected the past three weeks, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Tuten's Week 12 matchup is outstanding (Tennessee), but it's best to temper expectations to high-end fantasy RB2 levels. -- Cockcroft

Denver 38, Las Vegas 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
How much can rookie RB Jonah Coleman help fix what ails this Broncos offense? Yes, the Broncos won -- again. They made it far more difficult than it needed to be -- again. But an offense in desperate need of something to lean on found a spark with the blunt force of Coleman. Just when the Raiders looked as if they were poised for an upset after tying the score at 17-all, the Broncos leaned on Coleman. He had seven carries for 47 yards on the ensuing two drives, closing out each with touchdowns -- two of his three in the game. The rookie finished with his first career 100-yard game.

Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph wasn't happy this past week with an otherwise ferocious defense's penchant to surrender too many big plays. He said he even surprised the team when it returned from the bye with how angry he still was. Don't look for his smile to be back, because the Broncos surrendered three plays of over 30 yards Sunday, including a 68-yard catch-and-run touchdown by RB Ashton Jeanty. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: at Steelers (Friday, 3 p.m. ET)

Raiders
Should the Raiders consider making a change at cornerback? The Raiders have alternated among Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter and Hezekiah Masses at CB2. But should Las Vegas consider benching veteran Eric Stokes? His performance has declined after signing a three-year, $30 million extension in the offseason. He entered Week 11 allowing 35 catches for 435 yards and a passer rating of 112.6. And Denver QB Bo Nix especially picked on Stokes on Sunday. He gave up an 18-yard catch to WR Jaylen Waddle, setting up RB Jonah Coleman's second of three rushing touchdowns. Stokes' play should warrant conversations about a switch, especially after coach Klint Kubiak called out his effort last week. At the same time, would Porter or Masses be any better?

What to make of the QB performance: Mendoza held his own in Denver until the final drive, when he threw a pick-six to solidify the Raiders' seventh loss. He completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three touchdowns without his top pass catcher, Brock Bowers (ankle/quad). Mendoza helped the Raiders wipe away a 17-point deficit. And in the fourth quarter, he orchestrated an eight-play, 69-yard scoring drive to make it a one-score game. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Browns (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman's 34.9 points were a career high and the second most of any player through the late window. Coleman had 111 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries; he finished with four receptions for 18 yards. With three straight games of 18-plus points (and at least 15 touches) and a Week 12 matchup versus the Steelers, managers can play Coleman as a midtier RB1. -- Bowen

N.Y. Jets 27, L.A. Chargers 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jets
The Jets snapped a five-game losing streak, but was it worth it? Not according to the pro-tank crowd, which watched the Jets all but ruin any hope of landing the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. Their chances dropped to 1%, per ESPN Analytics. Draft ramifications aside, this was a much-needed win for the Jets (3-8), who matched their 2025 win total with their best offensive performance of the season. Quarterback Geno Smith was nearly flawless as the Jets scored on their first five possessions, ending their TD drought at 10 quarters. A win against a bad team requires proper perspective, but this is certain: They haven't quit on embattled coach Aaron Glenn.

Key stat to know: Wide receiver Sterling Shepard, 33, has been around a long time (11 seasons), but this was the first time he made two touchdown receptions in one game. He was elevated from the practice squad Saturday because of injuries at the position, and he responded with one of the best games of his 120-game career. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
How much did QB Justin Herbert miss WR Ladd McConkey? Just a week after the Chargers won their first game of the season, they never led in a three-point loss to the Jets. But the connection between Herbert and McConkey, who returned after missing two games because of a back injury, was a positive one for the Chargers as they rallied in the fourth quarter. In an offense that has struggled to find impact on the perimeter, McConkey had his third career game with two-plus receiving touchdowns. He entered Sunday's game with one receiving TD this season across six games.

Key stat to know: Sunday's matchup marks the first time Herbert finished a game with more passing touchdowns (two) than interceptions (zero) since a Week 16 win over the Cowboys in 2025. He went 11 straight starts -- including the playoffs -- with at least as many interceptions as passing TDs, per ESPN Research. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: It's been a frustrating season for Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's fantasy managers, but if you've kept your team in the race despite his NFL team's struggles, don't rule out his potential contributions to your stretch run. Over the past two weeks, he has 27.8 fantasy points -- 42 more rushing yards than expected and 6-of-36 carries going for 10-plus yards. That's production that meets the RB2 tier cutoff. -- Cockcroft

Carolina 35, Baltimore 33
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Panthers
Is the Panthers' offense good enough to help them run away with the NFC South? The division-leading Panthers got into a shootout with the slumping Ravens, who had lost five consecutive games coming into Sunday. Led by QB Bryce Young and RB Chuba Hubbard, the offense scored on six different drives. Hubbard, in particular, continued to show why he's the engine that can make big plays on offense, posting his second consecutive two-touchdown game. He has surpassed 100 all-purpose yards in five of the past seven games.

Most surprising performance: CB Will Lee III made a big impact in his return to the lineup. In the first half, the 2026 fourth-round pick took points off the board when he forced a fumble on RB Justice Hill for a touchback. In the fourth quarter, he hit the ball out of RB Derrick Henry's hands, and LB Tyrel Dodson recovered. He finished with four tackles, a pass breakup and two forced fumbles. -- Mike Kaye

Best quote from the locker room: ​When asked if Young's game-winning drives ever get old, DT Derrick Brown said: "Hell no. The goal is to win [laughs], so I'm not going to apologize to no damn body for f---ing how we win. If it takes until the last second, that's what it is."

Next game: at Buccaneers (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Is this the worst Ravens team in recent memory? It's certainly the sloppiest. In losing its sixth straight game, Baltimore was a mess in all three phases. The Ravens' offense committed three turnovers: a game-sealing interception by QB Jacoby Brissett, a fumble by RB Derrick Henry and a fumble by RB Justice Hill. The defense gave up 30 points for the fourth time in five weeks. And on special teams, punt returner LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts. The Ravens are technically still alive for the postseason, falling 2.5 games back of the AFC's last playoff spot. But there's not much faith remaining.

Key stat to know: Without Lamar Jackson (right thumb), the Ravens found other ways to score, becoming the first team in a decade to record a safety and score a kickoff return touchdown in the same game. The last team to do so was the 2016 Chiefs. In the first half, Baltimore got the safety off Mike Green's sack and got the touchdown off Devontez Walker's third career kickoff return. -- Jamison Hensley

Best quote from the locker room: ​Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton on the frustration level of the team: "I don't know if I have been a part of something like this -- definitely not losing six straight. I really don't know what to say at this point, honestly. I've told you everything I could tell you. I'm sure it's tough to come up with new questions at this point and it's tough to come up with new answers. So we're at where we're at."

Next game: at Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Panthers RB Chuba Hubbard continued his clear fantasy RB1 campaign with his fifth game of 20-plus carries and fourth of 24-plus fantasy points in his past seven games. Unfortunately, he has his two most challenging matchups up next: vs. the Buccaneers (Week 12) and Vikings (Week 13). Hubbard's usage props him up as a universal start, but we might be looking at scores in the teens. -- Cockcroft

Chicago 21, New Orleans 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bears
How does Ben Johnson get more of out the offense? Sunday marked Chicago's third win this season despite committing two turnovers, and the offense has yet to figure out how to put teams away early. The Bears need more from their run game after Zavion Thomas' end-around accounted for 30 of their 146 rushing yards. They also need more explosive plays across the board (QB Caleb Williams averaged 6.6 yards per pass). On Thursday, the Bears begin a brutal seven-game stretch vs. four divisional opponents, Jacksonville and Buffalo. To conquer the NFL's hardest remaining schedule, they'll need to get back to looking like the version that beat the Seahawks, Patriots and Falcons.

Most surprising performance: Thomas, a third-round rookie, saw his highest usage on offense all season and recorded a team-high 56 receiving yards on two catches. His speed adds another dimension, which Chicago utilized on the aforementioned reverse, and should earn him more playing time. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: at Lions (Thursday, 1 p.m. ET)

Saints
Has quarterback Tyler Shough regressed? It has been a tough stretch of games for Shough, who had fewer than 250 passing yards for the second straight game. He also threw an interception for the second straight game and was sacked for a safety. He has been sacked 14 times in the past three games. There are circumstances around Shough's struggles: He was playing with broken bones in his left hand, his starting center and starting right tackle are hurt and the run game has been one of the worst in the league. But the second-year QB has also had a hand in it with some poor decision-making.

Trend to watch: Turnovers, again. CJ Donaldson lost a fumble early in the game, the 11th fumble lost by the Saints this season, which leads the NFL and is only one fumble away from tying last season's total. The Saints were tied for the second-most fumbles in the league last season. -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: The Bears' backfield is truly struggling, even with RB Kyle Monangai back in action. D'Andre Swift was held to fewer than 12 fantasy points for a second straight game and fewer than 4.0 yards per carry for a fifth straight; Monangai scored 1.8 points and averaged 2.3 yards per carry. It's difficult to get behind Swift as more than a low-end fantasy RB2, and Monangai is a matchups-oriented flex. -- Cockcroft

Philadelphia 19, Pittsburgh 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles
Can the defense lead the Eagles on a mini-run? The defensive line has rounded into form the past two games. They sacked Aaron Rodgers five times after posting five sacks and nine QB hits against the Giants two weeks ago. Edge Jonathan Greenard has been part of that surge with two takedowns in two games after having none before Week 9. It will be a step up in competition on Thanksgiving against Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, but with the Cardinals and Colts up after that, Philly could make things interesting in a down NFC East if the defense continues to shine.

Key stat to know: Saquon Barkley showed a flash of his 2024 form with a 38-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter. It was his 18th career rushing TD of 30-plus yards (including playoffs), passing Jim Brown and Chris Johnson for fourth most in NFL history. The Week 10 bye appeared to be helpful for Barkley, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury. -- Tim McManus

Best quote out of the locker room: When asked about DK Metcalf's history with disqualifications, Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean said: "I didn't know how many ejections he had or whatever before going into it. But he wasn't getting the ball a whole lot during that game and some receivers could let that get to them. He obviously tried to take it out on me."

Next game: at Cowboys (Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET)

Steelers
Are the Steelers postseason contenders? The Steelers' record suggests they are, but the eye test says otherwise. With an immobile quarterback and a No. 1 receiver with more penalty yards than receiving yards, the offense is struggling. Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 in 10 days, has looked every bit his age recently; the Eagles sacked him five times Sunday. Meanwhile, DK Metcalf, who finished with one catch on four targets for 2 yards, was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. And with no threat of a passing game, the Eagles shut down the Steelers' run game. The defense eventually settled in, suggesting Pittsburgh might hold their own in the playoffs, but offensive ineptitude might keep it from even getting there.

Key stat to know: Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half -- the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking the stat in 2006. Of his 20 first-half attempts, 12 were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage, and his furthest attempt downfield was for just 8 air yards, per ESPN Research. -- Brooke Pryor

Best quote out of the locker room: Tight end Pat Freiermuth discussed Metcalf's second-half ejection from the game, saying his teammate "knows that's unacceptable. ... He'll be fine." Freiermuth continued: "He's one of my closest [friends] on the team. And so he knows that I have his back in those situations, but it just can't happen."

Next game: vs. Broncos (Friday, 3 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley scored 13.5 points, rushing for 75 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. He looked explosive on his 38-yard touchdown run, but he also struggled to find daylight at times. Barkley has a favorable upcoming schedule (@DAL, @AZ, IND), but with limited receiving upside (zero receptions in back-to-back games), he should be viewed as a risk/reward RB2. -- Bowen

Detroit 31, Tampa Bay 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Can the Lions' defense keep delivering without an injured Aidan Hutchinson? The Bucs' offense is not a strong group, so this wasn't the best test. But it was hard to know what to expect from the Lions after they lost their best defender to a season-ending knee injury. Detroit limited Tampa Bay's potent rushing attack and sacked quarterback Baker Mayfield four times. Thanksgiving, however, presents a much tougher test, as the Lions prepare to face the Bears. Chicago has scored at least 20 points in all but two games this season.

What to make of the QB performance: Jared Goff was stellar against the NFL's fourth-ranked defense by ESPN's FPI metric. He threw for 279 yards and two touchdowns while showing more mobility than we usually see from him. Goff eluded rushers and took only one sack despite the Bucs' complex blitz scheme. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Bears (Thursday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
With Sunday's loss, how important is next week's game against the Panthers? After winning two in a row, Tampa has now dropped two straight and sits at 3-7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers in Week 7, so a sweep would do wonders for a team whose season is slipping away. On Sunday, the Bucs didn't turn the ball over, but some untimely penalties (RB Bucky Irving had an 80-yard touchdown called back because of a holding penalty) and sacks proved costly. At least there was a bright spot in rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst III, who caught two touchdown passes.

Key stat to know: Irving rushed for a touchdown for a fourth straight game, which marks the longest streak by a Buccaneers player since Earnest Graham had six straight in 2007, per ESPN Research. Irving had two more touchdowns before the streak this season. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Panthers (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: After scoring a career-best 22.6 points, Buccaneers rookie WR Ted Hurst III should be viewed as a potential roster add. He caught 5 of 7 targets, finishing with 56 yards and two touchdowns. Plus, Hurst has the physical traits and speed to win boundary matchups. -- Bowen

Dallas 51, Tennessee 30
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys
What does beating the one-win Titans mean for the Cowboys' playoff hopes? The Cowboys did what they had to do by beating the Titans. You can scoff at that, but this is a team that lost at home to a then-winless Tampa Bay and a then-two-win Arizona team. The Cowboys' offense was unstoppable -- six touchdowns in their first six possessions -- albeit against a bad defense. Speaking of bad defenses, the Cowboys were incrementally better with Mike Pettine replacing Christian Parker as the playcaller, but they allowed two third-quarter touchdowns, including a 59-yarder when two defenders failed to touch WR Carnell Tate down on the ground. This has to be the formula if the Cowboys want to make it interesting in December.

Key stat to know: CeeDee Lamb is closing in on another No. 88. Lamb surpassed 1,000 receiving yards Sunday, giving him six straight seasons with 1,000 yards. Only Hall of Famer Michael Irvin, another No. 88, has more in Cowboys history with seven. Lamb also had the 50th touchdown catch of his career, tying him for sixth most in team history. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. Eagles (Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET)

Titans
Is this the worst Titans defense ever? The Titans allowed touchdowns on the first six drives by Dallas. The pass rush was virtually nonexistent, and the secondary was unable to cover anyone. The Cowboys rolled to 51 points, making Tennessee the third team since the 1970 NFL merger to allow 40 or more points in four consecutive weeks. This is the second Titans unit to do so, joining the 2004 Titans, who allowed 439 points. This season's Titans have given up 290 points and are on pace for 493. That would be a record for most points allowed by any Titans defense in a season, surpassing the 478 allowed last season.

Key stat to know: The Titans' defense allowed points on 13 straight drives. Per Elias Sports Bureau, that's the longest such streak by any team in a single season since 1978, when full play-by-play data became available. The previous longest streak was 11 straight drives allowed by the Chargers in October 2000. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Titans QB Cam Ward scored 22.22 points, throwing for 248 yards and two scores -- he also had a rushing touchdown. With 19 or more points in three straight games, and his upside as a runner (39 or more rushing yards in two of his past three games), Ward can be played as a QB2/superflex option. -- Bowen

Buffalo 26, Miami 9
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
Will the Bills keep passing like this? Buffalo attempted more passes in the first three quarters on Sunday than it had in any game since Week 1 of 2025. With a crucial stretch of potential playoff previews ahead, starting on Thanksgiving against Kansas City, the Bills just displayed their willingness to let Josh Allen throw the ball 45 times. How much of this is schematic evolution versus gamesmanship (in giving the Chiefs something to think about) is the real question.

Most surprising performance: Coach Joe Brady's decision-making. The Bills rolled the dice with a fake punt early in the first quarter while backed up in their own territory, and then inexplicably lined up for an onside kick up 14 in the fourth quarter. That's not to mention the aforementioned pass-first tactics. -- Nick Suss

Best quote from the locker room: "You guys know, sometimes I wish he wasn't as tough," said Brady on D.J. Moore's value to the Bills. "It pains me to say that. But he's kind of like Josh: When he gets tackled I just hope he gets up because of how important he is. He's as tough as they come."

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
Are the Dolphins a better team than their record suggests? On one side of the ball, yes. The defense isn't setting the league on fire, but since their Week 6 bye, they rank top-15 in sacks and top-five in takeaways (grabbing two Sunday). They held two of the top scoring offenses -- the Lions and Bills -- to under their season averages. However, Miami's offense averages the fewest points per game in the NFL and is the driving factor in the team's 1-9 record -- especially without QB Malik Willis. The Dolphins are destined for a top-five draft pick, but their defense has done enough to warrant optimism.

Trend to watch: After intercepting Allen twice, the Dolphins have now taken the ball away in six straight games. Taking it a step further, their rookie class has forced a turnover in all six games, and they're responsible for nine of the team's 11 takeaways this season. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Bills WR DJ Moore might have had his share of injuries this season, but he's quite a good fit as QB Josh Allen's No. 1 receiver when healthy. Moore's 23.1 fantasy points and 10 targets were both season bests, and he has at least 16 points in three of his past four games. He's a fantasy WR2 for a competitive stretch of upcoming games (KC, @NE, @GB, CHI, @DEN). -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 34, Arizona 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Are the Chiefs ready for the most difficult stretch of the season? After Sunday, the Chiefs appear to be ready. The team is optimistic running back Kenneth Walker III (groin), right tackle Jaylon Moore (right ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) will all be in the lineup for the Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills. That game starts the lone stretch this season in which the Chiefs will play consecutive road games -- against the Bills, Rams and Bengals. Those three games will likely determine if the Chiefs win the AFC West, and if they stay in the race for the AFC's top playoff seed.

Key stat to know: With two receiving touchdowns, tight end Travis Kelce passed Jimmy Graham for the fourth-most touchdowns (90) by a tight end in NFL history. Kelce also passed Rob Gronkowski for third place for the most total touchdowns (110) -- regular season and playoffs -- by a tight end in league history. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
Is it time for the Cardinals to start focusing on next season? As long as rookie Carson Beck is out, yes. The Cardinals' offense is a shell of former itself, and that has nothing to do with Josh Johnson at quarterback. They are starting an easier stretch to end the season that could give them a better chance to evaluate whoever is left to evaluate, which isn't a long list after all the injuries they have suffered. However, if Beck can return at some point this season, then the next six games will give Arizona plenty of time to get a long look at him and decide whether he's their quarterback in 2027.

Key stat to know: Arizona's second-quarter touchdown was its first in 21 drives, which covered two full games -- the loss to the Seahawks, in which they scored just three points, and the Rams loss last week, in which they scored just six points. All nine points were scored on field goals. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: vs. Commanders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Chiefs TE Travis Kelce scored more fantasy points in this game's first half than he did in any full game since Week 7 of 2023, showing he can still contribute top-shelf production to fantasy managers. He should be a big part of the Chiefs' passing game in upcoming matchups against the Bills (Week 12) and Bengals (Week 14) as well. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Heeney headlines returning Swans at pre-season training
stories.summary: After months of off-field turmoil in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal, the Sydney Swans have welcomed back four AFL players for pre-season training.
stories.body:
The Sydney Swans have welcomed back their embattled AFL quartet to training after months of off-field turmoil following the Pullman Hotel scandal.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice signalled their intent to resurrect their playing careers by taking part in the club's first-to-fourth-year pre-season training on Monday.

High-profile forward Tom Papley was also in attendance at Sydney's Bat and Ball Oval after being slapped with a three-game ban by the AFL for a positive roadside drug test.

Monday's session marked the first time Heeney, Warner, Bice and Jordon have officially trained with the Swans since serving a season-ending suspension for what the club termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

That AFL-endorsed suspension was also served by now-North Melbourne player Nick Blakey.

Separate from the bans, Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey were under investigation after three women made reports of sexual assault to Victoria Police.

Police have since confirmed the players would not be charged due to insufficient evidence.

Civil claims are still being prepared against relevant parties.

Monday's session was a relaxed affair, with the club also welcoming draftees Caylen Murray, Mason McGroder, Mitchell Knevitt and Brady Wright.

Players undertook the usual pre-season conditioning programs, doing running drills before moving on to contest work and a short match simulation.

It wasn't the first time Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Rice had trained with teammates, having done informal sessions at Centennial Park.

Papley, one of the team's most experienced players, returned to training as he prepares to face Waverley Local Court for driving with a suspended licence on November 26.

The 30-year-old was pulled over by NSW Police for a random roadside drug test on November 2, with checks revealing his licence was suspended due to non-payment of a parking fine.

The initial roadside test returned a positive reading, and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken.

That secondary sample returned a positive roadside test for the presence of cocaine and MDMA.

On top of his AFL ban for conduct unbecoming, Papley was fined $722 by police and his licence will be suspended for three months.

Papley spent most of Monday's training session with the rehabilitation group alongside fellow forwards Logan McDonald and Hayden McLean after undergoing surgery on both knees.

He suffered a grade-two medial collateral ligament strain in his right knee in the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, before undergoing an arthroscopy on his left knee to address a historic issue.

Papley will miss all pre-season matches and the club's opening rounds against Geelong, Essendon and GWS.

stories.headline: What Tarik Skubal's massive deal means for Mets, suitors, all of MLB
stories.summary: The two-time Cy Young winner is now baseball's highest-paid pitcher. Here's how Skubal's contract impacts the league.
stories.body:
Tarik Skubal is officially headed to the New York Mets on a record-setting $450 million contract. Skubal pitched the final months of the 2026 MLB season with the Los Angeles Dodgers following a midseason blockbuster trade from Detroit, where he had previously spent his entire career. After a free agency that earned interest from plenty of contenders, the superstar ace decided on the Mets on Sunday, ending his stay in L.A.

His nine-year, $450 million contract is now the largest in major league history for a pitcher. How does it change New York's outlook for 2027 -- and beyond? Where should the Dodgers and other suitors turn now? And what does it mean for baseball ahead of the impending lockout?

Our MLB experts weigh in on Skubal's sport-altering deal.

What is your initial impression of Skubal's $450 million deal ahead of the expected lockout?
Buster Olney: The contract numbers landed around where many in baseball believed they would, and it's not a surprise that it came down to the Mets. They were desperate to sign him; owner Steve Cohen had negotiated a monster deal with Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, before; and Cohen is one of the few owners -- maybe the only one -- seemingly unconcerned with the potential financial ramifications for his team if baseball's financial system changes dramatically under a new collective bargaining agreement. It was as if Captain Cohen shouted, "Damn the salary cap torpedoes, full speed ahead!"

Skubal gets paid, a little more than a week before the lockout deadline. But it appears more and more likely that 200-plus free agents will go without deals before the next CBA is forged.

Jeff Passan: The best pitcher in baseball went to the team that boasts spending near the top of the game. The deal is a microcosm of the conflict between the players and Major League Baseball over a salary cap, and the free market spoke to Skubal's actual value compared to the artificial limit the league intends to impose on individuals alongside its team-payroll cap. The Mets acted in their best interests, and it's hard to blame them. Even if a cap is in place, three stars on high-priced contracts can work in New York -- Skubal, Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor account for around $140 million of the league's projected $280 million cap in 2028 -- as long as their system churns out talent such as Nolan McLean, Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing. And if there isn't a cap -- and players aren't going to stop fighting against one specifically because contracts like Skubal's help salaries rise -- then the Mets will keep operating with a singular purpose: win the franchise's first World Series in more than 40 years.

What does it mean for the Mets to get an ace for the next nine years?
Jorge Castillo: They finally have a true No. 1 starter. Nolan McLean has ace potential, and he might reach it next season after a promising rookie year, but the Mets under president of baseball operations David Stearns have not employed a proven top-shelf starting pitcher. That's largely because Stearns prefers not to give free agent starting pitchers long-term contracts. The only other long-term contract the Mets have offered to a free agent starter under Stearns was Yoshinobu Yamamoto three years ago. But Yamamoto was 25. Skubal just turned 30. He has undergone three surgeries on his left elbow. This is not a Stearns move -- it's a Steve Cohen move, and it will bolster a rotation that has been a problem the past two seasons.

Alden Gonzalez: It means they have a tone-setter for their rotation, to go along with Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor as the faces of the position-player group. Skubal is arguably the best pitcher in the world -- and he's also someone McLean, Jonah Tong, Christian Scott and Jonathan Santucci can follow. David Stearns still has a lot of work to do with his roster, but he now has a foundation from which to build out the rest of his pitching staff.

What else can New York do to have a perfect offseason from here?
Bradford Doolittle: More. The Mets need more offense, more walks, better defense, more pitching. Of all that, getting a legit power-and-patience hitter at first base would be at the top of my list. Who? Maybe one of the overseas guys, Teruaki Sato (somewhat pricey to sign) or Koo Ja-wook (probably not expensive to sign). You can always juggle corner players, so you can't get too hung up on the first-base qualifier.

David Schoenfield: I'm with Brad on upgrading first base -- even though Jorge Polanco and Mark Vientos are still on the roster. If you want to believe in Ty France's 2026 resurgence, he's another possibility (and a good defender as well). He's risky given his age (32) and 2023-25 performance, but he did make some changes that helped him improve his exit velo and launch angle. Otherwise: bullpen. It wasn't terrible in 2026, but a quick scan of the roster doesn't exactly inspire confidence either. If money is no object -- and it apparently isn't -- Adrian Morejon is a must.

Where should Skubal's other suitors turn this offseason after missing out on the ace?

Gonzalez: The Los Angeles Dodgers wanted Skubal back, but they never got to the point of making an offer, according to sources. The potential of a salary cap and the general uncertainties of baseball's economic model with the collective bargaining agreement set to expire made them reluctant to make the type of long-term commitment it took to land him. The extent to which a federal investigation into Mark Walter's finances had an impact is unknown, though it has surely been heavily speculated upon. The Dodgers would still like to add a starting pitcher to address some of the volatility in a rotation fronted by Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani and Tyler Glasnow, three players whose workloads are always uncertain. They have Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Roki Sasaki and Gavin Stone behind them -- and Yamamoto, too, of course -- but look for them to add another starter regardless.

Castillo: Freddy Peralta fits the Toronto Blue Jays well for a few reasons. One is that his fastball would play up at Rogers Centre. We saw Peralta turn his season around upon getting traded to the Tampa Bay Rays at the deadline. That was partly, in addition to a few mechanical and pitch mix changes, because his fastball has more induced vertical break indoors, and the Rays call Tropicana Field, the only fixed-roof ballpark in the majors, home. "Fastball Freddy" combined that with an increase in velocity to salvage his platform season. Rogers Centre has a retractable roof. A lot of his starts would be inside. That matters. And it matters that the Blue Jays are willing to spend top dollar to further improve their rotation after giving Dylan Cease a seven-year, $210 million contract last winter.

Gonzalez: That the San Diego Padres were in on Skubal was an indication of how financially committed the new ownership group might be to bringing San Diego its first championship, but they were always better off spreading that money out to several pitchers. The Padres don't just need an ace -- they need several proven starters. At the moment, the only one in their rotation is Randy Vasquez, with Joe Musgrove and Yu Darvish both mysteries heading into 2027. So far this offseason, they've been in on practically everybody. And it would be a shock not to see them come away with multiple starting pitchers before the expected Dec. 1 lockout. The Padres need to address first base and left field, and ideally they'd also add to the back end of their bullpen, but starting pitching is by far their biggest priority. Look for them to get aggressive there now that Skubal is off the board.

What does this signing do to the 2027 playoff picture in both leagues?
Jesse Rogers: The balance of star power in MLB might have switched coasts but not leagues, as Skubal heading to the Mets keeps the National League an arm's length ahead of the American League heading into 2027. It also allows for some optimism in Queens, where the Mets haven't been very productive on the mound lately. Now the NL East boasts aces in Skubal, Chris Sale (Atlanta Braves) and Cristopher Sanchez (Philadelphia Phillies), which should make for a good division race. That's assuming the Mets bounce back and Skubal gives them the boost they need.

On the other side of the NL, the Dodgers won't miss Skubal the way other teams might have if they'd lost him. They were good before he arrived. They're still good.

Doolittle: Probably not much in the AL. In the NL, the Mets leapfrog the Braves in the NL East, just behind Philadelphia, but all three are tightly bunched. And all three are way behind the Dodgers and remain well behind the Milwaukee Brewers. This signing does boost the Mets' playoff chances by 17%, up to around 59%. And that's just for Year 1. It's a major add.

stories.headline: Haas confirm Rafa Camara will finish 2026 season with the team
stories.summary: Brazilian driver Rafa Camara will complete the 2026 season with Haas ahead of his full rookie season in 2027, the team confirmed on Sunday.
stories.body:
Brazilian driver Rafa Camara will complete the 2026 season with Haas ahead of his full rookie season in 2027, the team confirmed on Sunday.

Formula 2 championship leader Camara took the place of ousted Esteban Ocon in Brazil and continued in the seat at this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

He will race for the team in Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6. The Ferrari junior had already been confirmed to be replacing Ocon in 2027, but the Frenchman's sudden sacking during the Mexico City Grand Prix accelerated his F1 debut.

Haas' decision will likely cost Camara the chance to be F2 champion. F1's main feeder series will finish its own championship four races spread across the schedule in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- Camara holds a slender seven-point lead over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, with Alpine junior Alex Dunne 18 points back.

Team boss Aayo Komatsu said the opportunity for Camara to embed further into the team was too good to turn down. "We're excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," Komatsu said.

"I'm delighted that Rafa's embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to all of us ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Haas had one other option if they had wanted Camara to finish off his F2 campaign -- reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa filled in for Ocon in Mexico City and scored a top-ten finish on his debut.

Camara will keep driving alongside fellow Ferrari junior Oliver Bearman in the final races. Although it is expected to be completed soon, Bearman has not had a new Haas deal confirmed yet.

Bearman is understood to be in talks with Ferrari about their wider plans for his career, mindful of what happens with him should Lewis Hamilton extend his stay with the team beyond 2027.

stories.headline: DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos
stories.summary: Vanessa DiBernardo joined an elite list on Saturday, scoring for Kansas City direct from a corner. Known in soccer circles as an Olimpico, here are some of the very best.
stories.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published on Oct. 2, 2025, and it has been updated after Vanessa DiBernardo's stunner in Saturday's NWSL championship finale.)

For a relatively simple sport, soccer is filled with novelties.

Outfield players don the gloves and go into goal when there's no other option, penalty takers attempt chipped "Panenka" spot kicks to varying degrees of success, goalkeepers sprint the length of the pitch to come up for last-minute corners -- and sometimes they even score. And every now and then, players will score directly from a corner kick.

Highly improbable, sometimes intentional, a goal scored in this way is known as a Gol Olimpico, an Olympic goal.

But how did these goals get their name? The history of the Olimpico is irrevocably intertwined with South American football and with one of its great rivalries: Uruguay vs. Argentina.

- New Premier League record set with eight injury-time goals

- From World Cup Willie to Ciao: Ranking every World Cup mascot

- NWSL has more money than ever, yet its biggest problems remain

On June 9, 1924, Uruguay won the Olympic gold medal in Paris after defeating Switzerland 3-0. Around the same time in June 1924, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) changed the laws around corner kicks, making goals scored directly from the corner legal. But it wasn't until Oct. 2, 1924, that these two pieces of information would combine to create the Olimpico moniker.

Following Uruguay's Olympic victory, they played a two-game friendly series with their South American neighbors Argentina. The teams played out a 1-1 draw in Montevideo in late-September before travelling to Buenos Aires.

The return match was suspended after four minutes due to the large crowd on the sideline and was rescheduled for Oct. 2. Argentina would eventually win the rematch 2-1, but the whole game was filled with controversy. La Celeste withdrew from the match with four minutes remaining and both sides accused the other of excessive aggression.

But the important part of this story happened in the 15th minute, when Argentina's Cesareo Onzari whipped in a corner and scored.

The audacity of the goal and La Albiceleste defeating the Olympic champions was the catalyst for local journalists to dub the goal an Olympic one. From then on, whenever other goals were scored in this fashion, they were described as like the one scored against the Olympians, and soon the label Gol Olimpico was applied to all such goals.

The Olimpico is stunning when it's intentional and sometimes comical when it's not. It really has no right to work considering where players are standing on the field, how much of the target they can see from that position and what they need to do to the ball to make it curve into the back of the net. Whether they dribble through at the near post or sail past everyone into the far corner, there's beauty in the curl of ball, the audacity, the incredulity. It's glorious.

Take Vanessa DiBernardo's opening goal in Saturday's NWSL championship game. The Kansas City Current were set on course for their first NWSL title thanks to DiBernardo's Olimpico in the 54th minute, with the ball curling over everyone's head to nestle into the far corner of the next.

From regular-season matches to finals, the Olympics and even the World Cup, here are some of the very best Olimpicos.

Vanessa DiBernardo, Kansas City Current vs. Washington Spirit | 2026 NWSL championship

Kansas City fans will never forget how the Current's first NWSL championship was secured thanks in large part to DiBernado's kick from the corner. Hang it in the Louvre.

Marcos Coll, Colombia vs. USSR | 1962 World Cup

The most impressive part of the first Olimpico to be scored at a World Cup is who Coll beat in the USSR goal: the legendary Lev Yashin.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Canada | 2012 London Olympics

When it comes to scoring an Olimpico at the Olympics, only one player in soccer history has managed the feat: USWNT icon Rapinoe.

Elise Kellond-Knight, Australia vs. Norway | 2019 Women's World Cup

The Matildas may have got knocked out of the 2019 Women's World Cup on penalties, but they'll always have Kellond-Knight's amazing Olimpico at the Allianz Riviera in Nice.

Leandro Carvalho, Ceará vs. Corinthians | 2019-20 Brazilian Serie A

Carvalho's Olimpico was cunning and spectacular, catching the defence sleeping and using the outside of his foot. What's more, it was scored in the 92nd minute to level the scores at 2-2 against São Paulo giants Corinthians.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Australia | 2020 Tokyo Olympics

Remember when we said that Rapinoe was the only player in soccer history to score an Olimpico at the Olympic Games? Well she's did it twice, repeating her 2012 stunner over eight years later in Tokyo.

Hakan Çalhanoglu, Internazionale vs. AS Roma | 2020-21 Serie A

Why is Çalhanoglu's goal against AS Roma -- in Rome -- so memorable? It's an Olimpico at the Stadio Olimpico of course! How good.

Kyra Cooney-Cross, Melbourne Victory vs. Sydney FC | 2020-21 A-League Women

In the 120th minute of the A-League Women Grand Final, 19-year-old Cooney-Cross stepped up to take a corner ... and wrote her name into Australian football folklore.

Katie Zelem, Manchester United vs. Leicester City | 2021-22 Women's Super League

Scoring one Olimpico is hard enough, but Zelem managed to do it twice in one game. What's more, Zelem scored an Olimpico in the match before this one too.

Katie McCabe, Republic of Ireland vs. Canada | 2023 Women's World Cup

In their first appearance at a Women's World Cup, captain McCabe made sure Ireland fans would never forget the tournament with this inspirational strike.

Christian Pulisic, AC Milan vs. Club Brugge | 2024-25 UEFA Champions League

USMNT star Pulisic called it "a bit of luck" at the time, but there's no doubting the quality of his strike for AC Milan in their 3-1 win over Club Brugge in last season's Champions League league phase.

Son Heung-Min, Tottenham Hotspur vs. Manchester United | 2024-25 Carabao Cup

No Olimpico list would be complete without Son's stunner that sent Manchester United packing in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup quarterfinals. The South Korea skipper's crazy 88th-minute strike was the perfect denouement of a topsy-turvy match that finished 4-3 after Spurs had been leading 3-0.

Ángel Di María, Rosario Central vs. Boca Juniors | 2025 Liga Profesional de Fútbol

Last, but certainly not least, is this beauty from Di María for Rosario Central in their 1-1 draw with Boca Juniors in September. The Argentina star has a habit of scoring from corners, with this one -- astonishingly -- his fourth Olimpico.
