stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Roman Kantserov scores his first NHL hat trick in the Blackhawks’ 6-3 win over the Canucks
stories.summary: — Rookie Roman Kantserov got his first NHL hat trick and added an assist as the Chicago Blackhawks used a four-goal first period to beat the Vancouver Canucks 6-3 on Sunday night.
stories.body:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia -- — Rookie Roman Kantserov got his first NHL hat trick and added an assist as the Chicago Blackhawks used a four-goal first period to beat the Vancouver Canucks 6-3 on Sunday night.


Frank Nazar extended his scoring streak to six games with a goal and an assist for the Blackhawks, who won back-to-back games for just the second time this season.


Tyler Bertuzzi had a power-play goal and two assists, and Dominic Toninato also scored. Patrick Kane added two assists and Drew Commesso made 22 saves.


Zeev Buium, Filip Chytil and Jake DeBrusk scored for the Canucks. Brock Boeser had an assist to extend his career-high points streak to 12 games (four goals, 12 assists).


Vancouver starting goaltender Nick Tolopilo gave up four goals on 11 shots before being replaced by Kevin Lankinen at 12:44 of the first period. Lankinen ended the game with 17 saves.


Nazar scored on a breakaway 35 seconds into the game. Bertuzzi made it 2-0 on a power play at 2:48.


Kantserov, on another power play, and Toninato made it 4-0 before Buium scored for Vancouver.


Chytil cut Chicago’s lead in half early in the second period when his pass went off Blackhawks forward Jordan Greenway’s leg and into the net. Kantserov restored the three-goal lead by deflecting defenseman Alex Vlasic’s shot past Lankinen.


DeBrusk made it 5-3 late in the period on a delayed penalty, lifting a puck over Commesso’s glove. Kantserov then completed his hat trick in the third period.


Both teams were missing key players. The Canucks were without center Elias Pettersson, while captain Connor Bedard didn’t dress for Chicago.


Chicago scored three goals on four power-play chances. The Blackhawks have scored power-play goals in six consecutive games, going 10 for 18. They had just five in their first 18 games.


Up next
Blackhawks: Visit the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday night.


Canucks: Open a four-game road trip in Detroit on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
stories.summary: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
stories.body:
Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.

In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game. Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.

On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks. It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.

Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.

Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

stories.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: Snaps on offense, defense
stories.summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
stories.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. The Jaguars have followed through on that, making the 2025 No. 2 overall pick a starter on defense and mixing him in where designed on offense.

He has started every game at cornerback and has played at least four snaps on offense in all but one game (Week 4 at Cincinnati). He has made big plays on both sides of the ball and had the best game of his career in Week 6, when he clearly showed what kind of threat he can be. Head coach Liam Coen has been consistent in saying that Hunter's offensive usage is fluid.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches, then absolutely will."

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 11 at New York Giants

Hunter played a season-high 73 total snaps (his previous high was 71 in Week 4 against Cincinnati) and a career-high six special teams snaps against the Giants. He played 61 snaps on defense and six on offense, where he touched the ball twice. He had one catch for 3 yards and one rush on an end around that gained 9 yards. It was a quiet day on defense, too, with just six tackles. Hunter has been returning punts in practice, but the Jaguars used Ameer Abdullah in that role against the Giants instead of Parker Washington.

Week 10 at Tennessee Titans
Hunter came up with his highlight play of the season so far with a diving interception of a Cam Ward pass in the first quarter. Ward scrambled to his right on third-and-8 from the Jacksonville 35-yard line and threw back toward the left side of the field for receiver Elic Ayomanor near the sideline, but Hunter snagged the ball and cradled it to his body with his left hand as he hit the ground.

"It was an unbelievable catch, unbelievable play," head coach Liam Coen said. "... Such a special play by obviously a special player."

The Jaguars turned that into an eventual field goal and 10-3 lead early in the second quarter. Hunter, who is tied with cornerback Jourdan Lewis with a team-high three interceptions, played 56 snaps on defense, five on special teams, and five on offense against the Titans. He touched the ball on three of those offensive snaps: An end around that gained 3 yards and two catches for 16 yards.

Week 9 at Baltimore Ravens
It was a quiet night for Hunter on defense -- five tackles on 44 snaps -- but a bad one on offense. Hunter played six snaps on offense and fumbled the only time he touched the ball. Hunter caught a receiver screen from Trevor Lawrence, and Ravens safety Malaki Starks knocked the ball loose 1 yard behind the line of scrimmage. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan recovered the ball at midfield, and the Ravens took over with 5:10 to play in the third quarter with the Jaguars ahead 20-3.

The turnover didn't hurt the Jaguars, though, because the Ravens then turned the ball over on downs four plays later, with tight end Mark Andrews fumbling the snap on fourth-and-1. Hunter was officially credited with one catch for minus-1 yard.

Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Coming off a Week 7 bye week, it was a relatively quiet day from Hunter -- in terms of stats, anyway. Hunter played 49 of the 60 total snaps on defense tallying four tackles. He played six snaps on offense with one rush for 5 yards and no catches on one target. A new wrinkle this week is that he played a season-high four snaps on special teams -- returning a punt for 1 yard and securing a fair catch on another.

Week 6 vs. Houston Texans in London
Hunter had the best game of his career against the Texans at Wembley Stadium, catching four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and also intercepting C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He's just the fourth player since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a receiving touchdown and interception in the same game and the first to do it since Philadelphia's Brian Dawkins in 2002. The touchdown and interception came on consecutive drives.

Per NFL Next Gen Stats, Hunter had 34 coverage snaps and limited the Texans to two catches on five targets. However, he also was hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone against Nico Collins that gave the Texans the ball at the 1-yard line late in the first half. Despite that, this was the first time Hunter has made a significant impact on both sides of the ball -- 58 snaps on defense and 9 on offense (season high) -- in the same game in his 13 career games.

Week 5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles in London
Hunter played every defensive snap (59) for the second week in a row and had six tackles (second-most on the team) and a pass breakup. He was penalized for defensive pass interference that wiped out a third-and-17 incompletion in the second quarter. It gave the Eagles the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line and Philadelphia running back Will Shipley scored two plays later.

On offense, Hunter played five snaps and touched the ball for the first time since Week 1, catching a 9-yard pass on second-and-7 from the Jaguars' 40-yard line. Parker Washington scored on a 51-yard catch-and-run on the next play.

Week 4 at Cincinnati Bengals
Hunter played every defensive snap (71) in a 22-17 win against the Bengals and had four tackles and two pass breakups. It's the first time in his career he's played every defensive snap and it was necessary because the Jaguars were down cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring) and Christian Braswell (knee) because of injury.

"He played his ass off today," head coach Liam Coen said.

Hunter, however, called his play "decent" and was disappointed that his interception got erased by a roughing the passer penalty on defensive tackle Arik Armstead.

"I like to criticize myself a lot harder," Hunter said. "My wife does, too. I still give up a catch today, so she's going to be on me about that when I get home."

Hunter didn't play at all on offense, the first time in his career that has happened. Coen said he didn't want to risk him getting hurt on that side of the ball because that would leave them down three cornerbacks. Hunter said he wasn't mad at that decision.

Week 3 vs. New England Patriots
In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

Week 2 at Denver Broncos
Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton. The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

"We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

"But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

Week 1 vs. Cleveland Browns
Hunter started at cornerback and played 27 snaps on defense (55.1% of total defensive snaps) and four on offense (7.1% of total offensive snaps) against the Browns. On offense, he had one carry for 3 yards on a jet sweep and one catch for 8 yards on a screen pass. He has had at least one catch in every game in which he played (eight games) to this point. On defense, Hunter was targeted once on defense which resulted in a Deshaun Watson completed a 4-yard pass to KC Concepcion.

stories.headline: VAR gives Charlotte late penalty in series-opening win over Chicago
stories.summary: Pep Biel scored off a rebound from his own penalty kick in the 11th minute of stoppage time after a handball on Jack Elliot to give Charlotte FC a 2-1 win over the Chicago Fire on Sunday.
stories.body:
BRIDGEVIEW, Ill. -- Pep Biel scored off a rebound from his own penalty kick in the 11th minute of stoppage time after a handball on Jack Elliot to give Charlotte FC a 2-1 win over the Chicago Fire on Sunday.

The win, which came on the last kick of the game at SeatGeek Stadium, was the first regulation playoff victory for Charlotte in club history.

Josh Cohen replaced starting goalkeeper Chris Brady late in stoppage time with a penalty shootout on the horizon and surrendered the winner after saving Biel's initial effort. Biel's goal was his first in his third postseason appearance.

Liel Abada put an end to a scoreless match three minutes into the second half when he assists from defender Henry Kessler and Ashley Westwood set him up for a header off a set piece for his first goal in his sixth postseason appearance.

Kessler collected his first assist in his first playoff match with the club after not contributing to a goal in six postseason matches with the New England Revolution. Westwood's assist was his first in his eighth playoff appearance with Charlotte.

Robert Lewandowski pounced on a ball in the penalty area to head home the equalizer in the 68th minute for the Fire in his first postseason appearance. Defender Jonathan Dean notched his second assist in four playoff matches and Philip Zinckernagel picked up his third in three postseason outings.

Kristijan Kahlina saved four shots for No. 5 seed Charlotte (16-10-9).

Brady finished with two saves and Cohen had one for fourth-seeded Chicago (16-12-7).

Chicago swept the regular-season series with a 2-1 victory at home to start August and a 1-0 victory on the road to close out September.

The Fire travel to Charlotte for the second game of the best-of-three series on Saturday.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this recap.

stories.headline: Way-too-early look ahead to the 2027 AFL Draft: 15 players to know
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years with the introduction of Tasmania. Who are the players to know? Jasper Chellappah has named 15 to keep an eye on next year.
stories.body:
On to the next.

The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years, with Tasmania's inclusion making for an expansion draft similar to that of 2010 and 2011. The Devils own picks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 in the first round, plus the first pick of each subsequent round as part of concessions.

The club will need to trade 5, 7, 11, and 13 or roll them into 2028 or 2029. That means the competition's 19th team will take 1, 3 and 9 to the draft next year.

Tasmania has also pre-listed some of the brightest talents in the crop. Axel Walsh, Baxter Sruk, and Jake Miller were all clear pick No. 1 contenders 12 months out from their draft, and will attend school in Hobart and play football in the VFL next year.

Five Tasmania-tied teens have been included in the ones to watch next year. Another three are club-tied, making 2027 the most compromised draft in AFL history. Twenty-three of the 46 prospects in the AFL Futures exhibition on Grand Final day were club-tied.

Perhaps the saving grace for 18 other clubs is the fact that 2027 has been touted as an elite draft class for some time. There's premium talent still in the open pool and another 12 months for more quality to emerge, with a heavy leaning towards midfielders.

With an extended 15 prospects given the club-tied nature of the class, this is ESPN's way-too-early look ahead to the best prospects in the 2027 AFL Draft.

1. Axel Walsh (Tasmania pre-list)

East Perth/Western Australia

RUC, 201cm

Another in the resurgence of premium ruck prospects in the draft, and perhaps the best. Walsh is a monster in the air; his best traits come with his aerial strength where he drifts back to intercept mark, pushes forward to stretch defences and dominates around the ground. He will fill out to become a true ruck size and is as close to Max Gawn as a prospect has been this decade. Walsh would be the pick one favourite if he wasn't pre-listed by Tasmania.

2. Baxter Sruk (Tasmania pre-list)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 185cm

Sruk has been a big game performer and consistent midfield standout in the Talent League. He's a physical on-baller that throws his weight around, impacts with his ball-winning and gets forward to kick goals in bunches. Sruk thrives in the heat of the contest and brings tenacity to Tasmania's list.

3. Jake Miller (Tasmania pre-list)

Western Jets/Vic Metro

FWD, 197cm

Miller is the leading key forward prospect next year. He enjoyed a stellar national championships as a bottom-ager, named to the All-Australian team as well as the Talent League All-Australian side. Miller is a brilliant mark with arms outstretched, able to take big contested marks in packs and secure the ball on long searching leads. He's a reliable set shot off his left foot and is an elite runner for his size. Tasmania has already pre-listed the immense talent.

4. Max Thompson

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 175cm

Thompson has played in varying positions and looked good but is clearly at his best inside 50. He's smart and crafty, puts speed on the game and is a wonderfully fluid kick of the ball. Thompson can get up the ground and beat his man back to goals, distribute off halfback or win his own ball. He's the type of versatile small forward that clubs will covet.

5. James Artemis

East Fremantle/Western Australia

MID, 177cm

A leading contender in the open pool, Artemis is the cousin of Essendon's Jaxon and will have suitors very early in the draft. He's a hard-nosed contested midfielder that can then link up transition with hard running and slick ball use. He's dogged with the ball up for grabs and then powers through contact to get it moving forward.

6. Koby Bewick (Essendon father-son)

Calder Cannons/Vic Metro

MID, 178cm

Modern footy suits Bewick down to the ground. The son of 1993 and 2000 premiership small forward Darren, the Calder midfielder has been thrown around in different positions but has all the traits to become an excellent on-baller. He's incisive with his movement and foot skills on the outside, and possesses the running base and work ethic to rack up a lot of the ball in transition. He comes alive in open space where he can run and carry and pick out targets inside 50, which could see him start his career off halfback or a wing. Bewick kicked two goals from 19 touches in his Futures outing.

7. Zemes Pilot (Port Adelaide NGA)

South Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID, 193cm

Pilot is an elite basketball talent as well, so it's a coup for footy that the 193cm forward is opting to pursue opportunities in Port's NGA. The uber-athletic tall forward is incredible to watch, soaring above packs to take epic marks, breaking ankles with sharp agility and kicking goals from ridiculous angles. He had a game last year in the SANFL U16s with 27 disposals and 9.4 in front of goals.

8. Jett Flower

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID/DEF, 183cm

Flower is the grandson of Melbourne legend Robbie, and one of the top open pool prospects in 2027. Boasting one of the best names to come through the pathways in some time, Flower is a classy outside midfielder with beautiful foot skills and a strong running base. He likely appeals to clubs as a rebounder out of defence with his competitiveness a feature behind the ball. Flower was best afield in the Futures game with 17 disposals and a goal.

9. Louis Salopek (Port Adelaide father-son)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID/FWD, 186cm

A genuine star of the crop, Salopek has been in the wars across the past year or so, enduring three separate incidents of a collapsed lung. He burst onto the scene for Vic Country in the U16s champs and plays with a high motor, tackling and pressuring through the midfield and pushing forward to hit the scoreboard. He's keen to get to the Power as the son of Steven.

10. Riley Stratford (Tasmania pre-list)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 188cm

A taller midfielder who still needs to build into his frame, Stratford has been part of some massive games in his junior career. He was a star for Brighton Grammar on the way to an inaugural APS title and can play on a wing or through the engine room with impact in the air. Tasmania has locked him away and he'll play for their VFL side next year.

11. Oscar Henwood

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

MID, 185cm

Henwood was a key contributor in the Power's Talent League flag and plays with great composure. He can try to bite off too much with his time in possession but is typically creative and uses it really well in space.

12. Harvey Chapman

Sturt/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Chapman is the lone key defender inside the top bracket of the draft 12 months out, though he plays a more natural role as a rebounder. The SA tall is an excellent kick and sets up play from the last line of defence with instructive ball use. He can intercept with his reading of the play and gets involved in attack up the field.

13. Sam Husband (Tasmania Academy)

Tasmania Devils/Allies

MID, 180cm

The Devils didn't pre-list Husband because they have priority access to Tasmanian in the draft. He's the premier Tassie prospect in their inaugural draft and will be the poster boy of local talent for the 19th team. He's already played two seasons of Talent League football and is at his best using his evasiveness and skills around stoppages.

14. Campbell Creyk

West Perth/Western Australia

MID, 182cm

Creyk surged into the first round mix this year as a contested beast through the midfield. He rips the ball out of stoppages and doesn't often lose one-on-ones, playing with a hard edge that will serve him well at the next level. He will need to round out his game on the outside to continue pushing up draft boards.

15. Taj Garrett

Sturt/South Australia

MID, 183cm

A hard-running midfielder, Garrett's thirst to find the ball and work to contests is an important facet of his game. He outworks opponents and gets forward of the ball to impact. He may play his best football off a wing in the AFL but will get ample exposure on-ball for Sturt next year.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
stories.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool.
stories.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool, insisting Leny Yoro's early challenge on Alexander Isak was "never a red card."

Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute by referee Sam Barrott for what was deemed a last-man foul that denied Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

The Reds went on to complete a comprehensive rout over the 10 men with further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz as Mauricio Pochettino's Red Devils reign got off to a miserable start at Anfield.

The new head coach said he took full ownership of the result but felt the Yoro sending off changed the course of the game, with his skipper in agreement and feeling the wrong decision had been reached.

The Portugal midfielder told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas
stories.summary: The long-standing Max Verstappen-George Russell feud boiled over in Las Vegas, where the victorious Dutchman took delight in his rival's misfortune.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen took immense pleasure in watching George Russell's Mercedes disappear from his rearview mirrors and go nose first into the barriers on the penultimate lap of Formula 1's Las Vegas Grand Prix. The four-time world champion made no effort to disguise his glee over team radio in the immediate aftermath and then, once he had gone on to win Saturday evening's race, doubled down in his derision of the Mercedes driver while speaking to the media.

"It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening," Verstappen said in a postrace news conference. "I was like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

The comments will likely fuel an already-heated rivalry between the two drivers -- not least because Verstappen didn't stop there. Speaking to Dutch broadcaster Viaplay soon after, he also took aim at Russell's ability behind the wheel and disappointing season, saying the 28-year-old Briton was "all talk off the track and a complete joke on it."

By the time Verstappen's comments were lighting up social media like a jackpot-winning slot machine, Russell had already finished his media duties in Las Vegas, meaning he will likely wait until the paddock reconvenes in Qatar next week to give his response. But based on the pair's history, it seems incredibly unlikely he will take the criticism lying down.

In a sport in which many of the competitors are now remarkably friendly -- to the point that six drivers holidayed together between this year's races in Azerbaijan and Malaysia -- the animosity between Russell and Verstappen is real. But how did the relationship between the two drivers, who have never been teammates nor fought head-to-head for a title, sour to this level?

'Princess George' and 'borderline violence'
The first sign of public animosity between the two drivers emerged following the sprint race at the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Russell and Verstappen collided while fighting for position in the opening corners of the race, with the contact punching a hole in the side of Verstappen's Red Bull.

Staring at the damage in disbelief after the race, Verstappen, who went on to finish ahead of Russell, confronted the Mercedes driver as he walked past him in parc fermé. When Russell brushed aside Verstappen's complaints, saying "I didn't have any grip," the 29-year-old Dutchman appeared genuinely insulted and retorted, "We all had no grip!" Russell then dismissively walked away from the argument, with Verstappen calling after him, "Expect next time the same, d---head!"

The drama was caught on one of F1's roving cameras in the pit lane, making the exchange the main talking point after the race. Speaking to Dutch journalists in the paddock, Verstappen labeled his rival "Princess George," while the Mercedes driver told TV crews he was genuinely "surprised" by how angry Verstappen had been.

If nothing had followed the Baku collision, the incident could have been written off as a one-off quarrel in the heat of the moment. But over the following years, it became clear there was a serious grudge from both sides.

The next time the spat went public was at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, where Verstappen was given a one-place grid penalty for driving slowly on a preparation lap in qualifying. The penalty moved Russell onto pole position, but Verstappen felt his rival -- who had to take evasive action around Verstappen while on a warmup lap of his own -- had gone out of his way to get Verstappen penalized in the stewards' room.

"I find it ridiculous how [he] wants to make sure I get a penalty," Verstappen said at the time. "You know what it is? He acts decent in front of the camera here, but when you talk to him personally, he is a different person ... I can't stand that. In that case, you can better f--- off."

A week later at the final round of the season in Abu Dhabi, Russell responded to Verstappen's comments, claiming the Dutchman threatened him with "borderline violence" after the stewards' briefing.

"I find his comments pretty ironic when he comes out and says, 'I'm going to purposefully crash into you, I'm going to put you on your f---ing head in the wall.' For me, that isn't acceptable and he's gone beyond the line here, and I'm not going to accept it," Russell said. "So somebody's got to stand up to a guy like this before it gets out of control.

"All of this is racing, but he's felt the need to take it personal. I have no idea why he's done that, and he cannot deal with adversity.

"Whenever anything is not going his way, he lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence. We've seen it in Brazil in the past with [Esteban] Ocon, we saw it in '21 with Lewis [Hamilton], in Mexico with Lando [Norris], in Budapest when he didn't have the most dominant car, crashes into Lewis, slamming his whole team. That is not a guy who I respect, and I wish he would be a better role model."

When Russell's quotes were put to Verstappen, it only upped the ante in the paddock's latest war of words.

"I didn't say it like that," Verstappen responded. "But you know, that's another thing. That happened behind closed doors, so you don't have to share everything that was said there and make it more dramatic.

"But you know, those things don't surprise me. I just give my opinion about how he is. Of course, he's not happy with it, but it's the same thing he did at the stewards. Lying and putting things together that aren't correct.

"He's a backstabber. It doesn't matter to me. You don't have to talk too much about people like that, they are just losers."

That same weekend in Abu Dhabi, the full F1 grid met for a dinner as part of an ongoing tradition among drivers to spend at least one evening per year as a complete group. Speaking on the "Pitstop" podcast later the same month, Liam Lawson told a story of how the weekend's bickering in the paddock spilled over to the dinner table.

"This is f---ing funny. It's really funny," Lawson said. "We rock up, at this big table. As the table was filling up, that side of the table was pretty much full, and opposite me was Max and then three chairs to the left [of him]. George hadn't turned up at this point.

"We all said, 'We're going to save the spot for George right next to Max.' George arrives and Max said, 'Mate, we've saved a seat for you.' And George just picks up the chair and walks to the other end of the table and sits with Lewis at that end of the table."

The next flashpoint came at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix, when Verstappen crashed into the side of Russell's car -- seemingly out of pure frustration. The collision happened shortly after a late safety car period had left Verstappen on worn tires in the fight against his rivals and scuppered his chances of a podium finish.

Russell attempted a move on Verstappen at Turn 1 that resulted in the Mercedes driver sliding into Verstappen, forcing the Red Bull driver off the track. The stewards launched an investigation into the incident, which Red Bull feared might result in Verstappen receiving a penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Verstappen's engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, radioed his driver to tell him to give the position back to Russell to avoid a potential penalty -- much to the frustration of Verstappen. On the approach to Turn 5 on the following lap, Verstappen appeared to cede the position to Russell, only to accelerate again before the apex and collide with the Mercedes.

The stewards deemed Verstappen entirely at fault for the collision and issued a 10-second penalty -- dropping him to 10th place at the finish -- as well as three penalty points on his superlicense, bringing him just a single point from a race ban. Although Verstappen later admitted the incident "should not have happened" in an Instagram post -- as close to an apology as you'll likely get from the Red Bull driver -- Russell still took the opportunity to take a sideways dig at his rival.

"I was a bit surprised to see him taking responsibility, because it's quite unlike him," he said. "We actually bumped into each other at the airport a few days ago, but we didn't even chat about it. He was there with his family and his newborn, chatting about how that was going. He was busy folding the pram and trying to get it through the security scanner.

"Had I been taken out of the race, I'd be feeling very differently for sure. Ultimately, his actions benefitted me, cost him, and I should say thanks."

The pair then lined up on the front row of the grid for the next race in Canada, leading Russell to make a pointed joke about how close Verstappen was to a race ban.

"We're mates so it's all good," Russell said when asked about the potential for a collision at the first corner. "I've got a few more points on my license to play with! So ... let's see."

Verstappen was said to be annoyed by the comments and another row broke out after the race when Red Bull tried to get Russell disqualified for driving erratically behind a safety car. Verstappen had briefly overtaken Russell when the Mercedes driver hit the brakes to warm his tires behind the safety car, and Red Bull protested the move following the race, only for the appeal to be thrown out by the stewards several hours later.

As an aside, but another example of Verstappen's tendency to hold a grudge, the incident with Russell at the Spanish Grand Prix was referenced in the postrace news conference at the season-deciding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. When a journalist asked Verstappen if he regretted the incident given that he lost the title by fewer points than the penalty cost him in Spain, the Red Bull driver responded, "You forget all the other stuff that happened in my season. The only thing you mention is Barcelona. I knew that would come. You're giving me a stupid grin now."

Nearly four months later, at this year's Japanese Grand Prix, Verstappen refused to start his news conference until the same journalist had left the room.

What happened in Vegas is unlikely to stay in Vegas
Coming back up to speed under the bright lights of Las Vegas on Saturday night, and Russell and Verstappen spent the first half of the race trading position at the front of the field -- invariably with Verstappen coming out on top.

Russell, who desperately needed a victory to salvage something from the most bruising season of his career, appeared to be overdriving each time he got his nose ahead of the Red Bull. If Russell took the lead into Turn 14, Verstappen always had an answer, whether it came through the high-speed Turn 17 on the following straight or by waiting for Russell to go deep at Turn 1 and retaking the position in Turns 2, 3 and 4.

Things got worse for Russell on lap 38 when he slipped behind teammate Kimi Antonelli to third place, meaning as the laps counted down, he needed to do something extra special to move up two positions and salvage victory.

With two laps of the 50-lap race remaining, he resorted to a high-risk, late-braking attempt on Antonelli at Turn 5. Only a few drivers had made such a pass stick all evening, and as Russell found himself off the racing line, a combination of debris and dust resulted in a lock-up and light contact with the barrier in the run-off area.

"Ha ha, well done! My God," Verstappen laughed over team radio as he watched events unfold behind him.

Russell managed to extricate his car from the barrier, but the time lost returning to the track meant he could only manage a ninth-place finish at the checkered flag.

Verstappen's desire to comment so publicly about Russell's misfortune was notable and no doubt at the front of his mind due to an incident between the two drivers during final practice in Las Vegas the day before.

A loose gentleman's agreement exists between drivers to wait in line to start a fast lap in practice, and Verstappen essentially tried jumping the queue ahead of Russell on the back straight toward the end of the session. Russell, aggrieved by the move, then attempted to repass Verstappen ahead of Turn 14 -- the last braking zone before the start of a new lap -- but in doing so was squeezed to the inside of the track by the Red Bull, resulting in a light brush of wheels between the two cars at the apex.

In the eyes of the stewards, the incident only warranted giving a warning to Verstappen for movement under braking, but in the furious microclimate of the Verstappen-Russell rivalry, it added fuel to the fire once more.

Speaking after the qualifying session that followed final practice, Russell built on his previous rhetoric that Verstappen acts like a paddock bully.

"I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

Immediately after qualifying, Verstappen refused to acknowledge the practice incident but couldn't resist sticking the knife in after his victory on Saturday. In an interview with Dutch broadcaster Viaplay, he was asked if the win had been in some way been inspired by Russell's quotes the previous day.

"His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me," Verstappen responded. "All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect karma."

The 2026 title battle may be over, but the drama in the F1 paddock never stops. Expect this one to continue at the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
stories.summary: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
stories.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.

Como previously said Kean needed treatment on an injury in practice after returning from national team duty.

In its first season in the Champions League, Como have adapted stunningly fast with a 9-1 win at Lens and a pair of 4-1 victories at home to Manchester United and RB Leipzig.

Como are fourth in the 36-team standings ahead of hosting AEK Athens on Tuesday. The league phase for Como finishes with Real Betis next month and titleholders PSG, one of Kean's former clubs, and Barcelona in back-to-back weeks in January.

Kean arrived at Como on an initial season-long loan from Fiorentina and his injury leaves just Tasos Douvikas as a proven striker until the January transfer window. Kean has been limited to just four appearances for Como so far this season.

Como are fifth in Serie A and host Cagliari on Saturday.

stories.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
stories.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
stories.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013.

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

'Breaking Bad' nears its end as 'Roar' rules the charts

One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out.

Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars.

Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010.

Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4.

The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem.

WNBA, MLB teams were building championship legacies

The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs.

MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however.

BCS era coming to a close

College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least.

One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign.

Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

stories.headline: First-half romp powers Jillaroos' fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup salute
stories.summary: Australia's Jillaroos have blown away New Zealand 34-10 to win a fourth-straight Women's Rugby League World Cup.
stories.body:
Australia have underlined their women's rugby league dominance with a 34-10 annihilation of New Zealand in the World Cup final.

The Jillaroos did the damage with six first-half tries on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, with winger Jaime Chapman recording a brilliant hat-trick before the break to cap a historic tournament.

It was Australia's fourth straight Cup triumph, following a 54-4 win in the final four years ago and coming after New Zealand won the first three tournaments between 2000-08.

Chapman carried two players more than 10 metres to score her first, before flying into the corner for another and then busting through four tacklers for a sensational 70-metre solo effort.

Her treble gave her the equal record for tries in a World Cup -- for men or women -- at 13, matching the Kiwi Ferns' Honey Hireme-Smiler from 2017.

It seemed inevitable that she would go clear in the second half.

But both teams struggled in the Brisbane humidity, with the Kiwi Ferns' try in the finals seconds the only points of an error-riddled second period.

For the Jillaroos there were several poignant narratives to come out of the win.

Coach Jess Skinner's controversial decision to play five-eighth Jesse Southwell and drop Jocelyn Kelleher paid dividends.

Southwell schemed with the ball, landed five goals and was the perfect foil for half Tarryn Aiken, who controlled play with confidence and skill.

Chapman played in the pool games and semi-final in the 2022 World Cup but has now put an indelible stamp on a final.

"There is no better win than winning the World Cup on home turf," she told Channel Seven.

"We connected the first day we came into camp."

Fullback Tamika Upton sat out the tournament four years ago with a calf injury but now the five-time premiership winner has every team accolade in the game to her credit.

Prop Millie Elliott retires with a fairytale ending while dual international Sariah Paki, who was chased by the Ferns to play for them, has now won the World Cup in two sports after triumphing with the Australian rugby sevens side in 2022.

All the talk before the clash was the danger posed by New Zealand's Golden Boot winner and strike centre Stacey Waaka.

The former rugby union star, who had scored nine tries in the tournament, was snuffed out by Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly, who confronted Waaka all match and gave her no space.

As the Jillaroos' big guns stood up, centre Jessica Sergis scored her 23rd try in 18 Tests with a 70m dash through the middle off an undetected forward pass.

Aiken turned second-rower Shaylee Bent inside for the second try of the match while Upton started and finished a movement that had her attacking fingerprints all over it.

Ferns fullback Apii Nicholls was her side's best player in a dynamic display until she tore a hamstring in the 66th minute.
